1: At Sinai Moses counts the men able to fight, tribe by tribe: over six hundred thousand. The Levites are counted separately for the tabernacle.
God knows his people by name and number.
2: Each tribe camps under its banner on one of the four sides, with the tabernacle in the middle.
God is at the centre of his people's life.
3: The Levites are given to Aaron to serve the tabernacle, taking the place of Israel's firstborn sons.
Some are set apart for God's service on behalf of everyone.
4: The three Levite clans receive their tasks for packing and carrying the tabernacle and its furnishings.
Every task in God's service has dignity.
5: The unclean are placed outside the camp, wrongs must be repaid, and a ritual is given for a husband who suspects his wife.
God lives in the camp, so its life must be clean and just.
6: The Nazirite vow and the blessing
Rules for those who vow special dedication to God: no wine, no cutting the hair. Then the priestly blessing: "The Lord bless you and keep you."
Samson and John the Baptist lived something like this vow. The blessing is still used today.
7: For twelve days the leader of each tribe brings identical offerings for the altar. Moses hears God's voice from above the ark.
Every tribe has an equal share in worship.
8: Aaron sets up the seven lamps. The Levites are cleansed and presented to God for service.
Those who serve must first be purified.
9: The second Passover and the cloud
Those who were unclean or travelling may keep Passover a month later. The people move only when the cloud lifts from the tabernacle.
Israel learns to follow God's lead day by day.
10: Two silver trumpets signal the camp. After nearly a year at Sinai, Israel sets out in order behind the ark.
The journey to the promised land resumes.
11: The people weep for the food of Egypt. Moses is worn out, and God shares his spirit with seventy elders. Quail arrive, followed by a plague.
Ingratitude makes slavery look attractive. Moses wishes all God's people were prophets.
12: They criticise Moses out of jealousy. God defends him as the one he speaks with face to face. Miriam is struck with leprosy, and Moses prays for her.
Moses is called the meekest of men. He prays for those who attack him.
13: Twelve men scout Canaan and return with huge grapes. Ten say the people there are giants and cannot be beaten. Caleb says, "We can do it."
Fear exaggerates the obstacles and forgets God.
14: The people refuse to enter and want to go back to Egypt. Moses pleads, and God forgives, but that generation will die in the desert. Only Caleb and Joshua will enter.
Unbelief costs a whole generation the promise.
15: Laws for offerings once in the land. A man who breaks the Sabbath is punished. The people wear tassels to remember the commandments.
We need visible reminders to keep God's word in mind.
16: Korah and 250 leaders claim the priesthood for everyone. The earth swallows the rebels. When the people still complain, a plague begins and Aaron stops it with incense.
Sacred office is given by God, not seized.
17: Twelve staffs are placed before the ark. Aaron's alone buds, flowers and bears almonds.
God himself confirms whom he has chosen as priest.
18: Priests and Levites are responsible for the sanctuary. They receive no land; the tithes are their share.
"I am your portion," God tells them. Those who serve the altar live from it.
19: The ashes of a red cow, mixed with water, cleanse anyone who has touched a dead body.
Hebrews says that if this purified the body, Christ's blood purifies the conscience far more.
20: Water from the rock; Aaron dies
Miriam dies. The people quarrel over water, and Moses strikes the rock twice in anger instead of speaking to it. He and Aaron will not enter the land. Aaron dies on Mount Hor.
Even Moses is held to account. Leaders must show God's holiness.
21: Poisonous snakes bite the complaining people. Moses lifts a bronze serpent on a pole, and whoever looks at it lives. Israel defeats two kings.
Jesus says the Son of Man must be lifted up in the same way.
22: King Balak hires the seer Balaam to curse Israel. On the road an angel blocks the way, and Balaam's donkey speaks to him.
No one can curse those God has blessed.
23: Twice Balak sets up altars for a curse, and twice Balaam can only speak blessing.
"God is not man, that he should lie." His word stands.
24: Balaam blesses Israel a third time and foretells, "A star shall come out of Jacob, and a sceptre shall rise out of Israel."
Christians have long read this as pointing to the Messiah and linked it with the star of the Magi.
25: Israelite men are drawn by Moabite women into immorality and the worship of Baal. A plague kills thousands until Phinehas acts.
What enemies could not do from outside, temptation does from inside.
26: A new generation is counted on the plains of Moab. Of those counted at Sinai, only Caleb and Joshua remain.
God's word about the desert generation has come true.
27: Five sisters with no brother ask for their father's inheritance, and God grants it. Moses lays hands on Joshua as his successor.
God provides for the overlooked and for the future of his people.
28: The offerings for every morning and evening, each Sabbath, each new moon, Passover and Weeks.
29: Offerings for the feast of Trumpets, the Day of Atonement and the eight days of Tabernacles.
The year itself is offered back to God.
30: A man must keep his vow. Rules are given for vows made by women within a household.
Words spoken to God are binding.
31: Israel defeats Midian, which had led it into sin at Peor. The plunder is purified and divided.
A hard chapter. It shows how seriously the Old Testament treats what leads the people away from God.
32: Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh ask to settle east of the river. Moses agrees on condition that they first help their brothers conquer Canaan.
No one should rest while their brothers are still fighting.
33: A list of every camp from Egypt to the plains of Moab. God commands Israel to drive out the Canaanites and destroy their idols.
Looking back, Israel can see God's guidance at every stage.
34: God sets the boundaries of Canaan and names a leader from each tribe to divide it.
The promise becomes concrete: real land with real borders.
35: The Levites receive forty-eight towns. Six are places where someone who kills by accident can be safe until trial.
Justice must distinguish accident from murder.
36: Daughters who inherit must marry within their own tribe so that each tribe keeps its land.
Each family's share in the promise is protected.
